observations: The authors describe adaptations as specific to the training stimulus, while noting carryover across muscular performance domains in nonadvanced trainees.

The discussion distinguishes initial benefit from continued longer-term progress: increasing a stimulus can support continued adaptation, but progression is not a prerequisite for every initial benefit.
The authors state that pooled group-level findings require individualization to goals, needs, experience and circumstances; the review does not predict each individual response.

The discussion reports uncertain overall strength conclusions, with one volume-equated review slightly favouring periodization. It does not establish a universal periodized-program advantage under appropriate overload.
The authors propose near-failure or a target of two to three repetitions in reserve as a way to achieve sufficient effort; completing every set to muscular failure is not required for benefit.
